# `sesam show --clip` diverts a secret to the clipboard instead of stdout and
# arms a detached `sesam unclip` that wipes it again once the TTL is up. The
# system clipboard is replaced by SESAM_CLIPBOARD_{COPY,PASTE}_CMD so this runs
# without a display server.

env CLIPBOARD_FILE=$WORK/clipboard
env SESAM_CLIPBOARD_COPY_CMD=$WORK/copy.sh
env SESAM_CLIPBOARD_PASTE_CMD=$WORK/paste.sh
# The unclip handover file lives here; keep it inside $WORK so parallel
# scripts cannot clear each other's clipboard.
env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$WORK/run
mkdir $WORK/run
chmod 0755 $WORK/copy.sh
chmod 0755 $WORK/paste.sh
chmod 0755 $WORK/preload.sh
chmod 0755 $WORK/wait-empty.sh
chmod 0755 $WORK/unclip-now.sh

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

exec sesam add token.txt --group dev

# Plain `show` must never touch the clipboard: it doubles as git's textconv
# driver and runs once per blob during `git diff`.
exec $WORK/preload.sh
exec sesam show token.txt
stdout 's3cr3t'
grep '^untouched$' $WORK/clipboard

# --wait and --ttl are meaningless without a clip flag.
! exec sesam show --ttl 10s token.txt
stderr 'require --clip'
grep '^untouched$' $WORK/clipboard

# --clip keeps the secret off stdout and strips the file's trailing newline,
# which would otherwise submit the form it gets pasted into.
exec sesam show --clip --ttl 0 token.txt
! stdout .
grep '^s3cr3t$' $WORK/clipboard

# --alsoclip does both.
exec $WORK/preload.sh
exec sesam show --alsoclip --ttl 0 token.txt
stdout 's3cr3t'
grep '^s3cr3t$' $WORK/clipboard

# --wait clears in the foreground once the TTL expires.
exec sesam show --clip --wait --ttl 10ms token.txt
! stdout .
! grep . $WORK/clipboard

# Without --wait the clear happens in a detached child that outlives us.
# Nothing is asserted between the copy and the clear: the child fires on its
# own schedule, so only the end state is deterministic.
exec sesam show --clip --ttl 100ms token.txt
exec $WORK/wait-empty.sh

# The remaining checks arm an unclip far enough in the future that it cannot
# fire on its own, and then drive it by hand.
exec sesam show --clip --ttl 10s token.txt
grep '^s3cr3t$' $WORK/clipboard

# An unclip whose token a newer copy superseded keeps its hands off.
exec sesam unclip --ttl 0 --token 0000000000000000
grep '^s3cr3t$' $WORK/clipboard

# A clipboard the user overwrote in the meantime is left alone too: the armed
# unclip only wipes content that still matches its digest.
exec $WORK/preload.sh
exec $WORK/unclip-now.sh
grep '^untouched$' $WORK/clipboard

-- token.txt --
s3cr3t
-- copy.sh --
#!/bin/sh
cat > "$CLIPBOARD_FILE"
-- paste.sh --
#!/bin/sh
cat "$CLIPBOARD_FILE" 2>/dev/null
-- preload.sh --
#!/bin/sh
printf %s untouched > "$CLIPBOARD_FILE"
-- unclip-now.sh --
#!/bin/sh
# Run the pending unclip right now, with the token the armed child was given.
state="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sesam/unclip.json"
token=$(sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([0-9a-f]*\)".*/\1/p' "$state")
[ -n "$token" ] || { echo "no token in $state" >&2; exit 1; }
exec sesam unclip --ttl 0 --token "$token"
-- wait-empty.sh --
#!/bin/sh
# Poll instead of sleeping for a fixed span, so the assertion fails loudly
# rather than flaking when the machine is busy.
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt 100 ]; do
	[ -s "$CLIPBOARD_FILE" ] || exit 0
	sleep 0.1
	i=$((i + 1))
done
echo "clipboard was not cleared within 10s" >&2
exit 1
